gen-fs-segment-fs-alpino: Segment is a commanding display face, with generous gaps between its letters and a tall middle band that looks stocky. Alpino follows in a cozy, casual sans, made for short stretches of reading, so the two feel like a firm voice and a friendly aside.
gen-fs-segment-montserrat: Segment stands up front with a stocky, tall middle band and wide gaps between letters, while Montserrat below stays geometric and approachable. Its line glides like wire.
gen-fs-sharpie-fs-chillax: Expressive and bold, Sharpie crowds its letters behind what feels like a narrow slot. Chillax loosens things with open, relaxed curves that never thin at the turns, and it is made for short stretches of reading.
gen-fs-sharpie-fs-public-sans: Public Sans has a hefty lowercase and broad open counters that feel trustworthy at a glance. Over a longer stretch it would read steadily, while Sharpie keeps its tight, hairline-gapped letters up top.
gen-fs-sharpie-fs-rowan: Sharpie brings bold, expressive letters packed with only a hairline of space between them, and Rowan answers underneath with a friendly literary serif. Sharpie earns its keep big and short, and Rowan is comfortable in small doses.
gen-fs-spline-sans-fs-literata: Rounded, nib-like strokes with no swelling at their ends give Spline Sans an approachable, geometric look. And Literata, a bookish text serif with sturdy hairlines and wide-mouthed curves, would carry a longer stretch of reading with a quiet, sophisticated pull.
gen-fs-stardom-fs-asap: Dramatic and bold, Stardom throws outsized lowercase with thick diagonals against hairline counter-strokes. But Asap, a readable plain sans with open arcs, is made for short stretches of reading, so a longer passage would feel plainer.
gen-fs-styro-fs-alpino: Alpino reads cozy and casual, with its curve endings kept well apart. Styro, the retro display heading, packs its letters tightly, so a longer passage would lean on Alpino while brief copy suits Styro better.
gen-fs-styro-fs-bespoke-sans: Bespoke Sans reads sharp and refined, with generous space where curves meet stems. Styro presses its letters close and does its best work as a commanding heading, while Bespoke Sans handles the quieter, open work underneath.
gen-fs-styro-fs-bespoke-slab: Bespoke Slab is a grounded, refined serif with tall bodies in every lowercase letter, not meant for long paragraphs. Bespoke Slab gets modest sizing, and Styro supplies the retro, commanding heading above it.
